clinician.trajectory_summary: A 61-year-old man presented with bilateral flank pain starting on the left side progressing to the right side, dyspnea on exertion, urinary frequency, foamy urine, and bilateral floater symptoms. He had a history of hypertension and newly diagnosed anterior uveitis confirmed by slit lamp examination with mild inflammatory cells in the anterior chamber without synechia. Laboratory evaluation revealed renal impairment with elevated serum creatinine (2.3 mg/dL), elevated BUN (26 mg/dL), and reduced estimated GFR (30.9 mL/min). Kidney biopsy confirmed tubulointerstitial nephritis demonstrated by diffuse interstitial infiltration of lymphocytes and eosinophils, mild tubular atrophy with focal fibrosis, absence of immune complex deposits on immunofluorescence and electron microscopy. These findings confirmed the diagnosis of tubulointerstitial nephritis and uveitis (TINU) syndrome.
